question:
An astronomical telescope is used in normal adjustment (final image at infinity). The objective has focal length $f_o=100\,\text{cm}$ and clear aperture diameter $D=5.0\,\text{cm}$. The eyepiece has focal length $f_e=5.0\,\text{cm}$. The observer’s unaided eye can just resolve two distant point objects if they subtend an angle at least $\alpha_0=3.0\times10^{-4}\,\text{rad}$.

Two distant stars are separated by an angle $\Delta\theta=2.0\times10^{-5}\,\text{rad}$ in object space.

Assume the telescope is diffraction-limited by the circular objective and use the Rayleigh criterion. Also, model the light as photons of energy $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$.

Find the minimum photon energy $E_{\min}$ (in eV) of the starlight such that the two stars can be just resolved by this telescope-eye system. (Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.)
